plain_description.what: Builds a separate tree for each of six benchmarks, each with its own certification, then grafts them under one root. The result is compared with a single tree built on all six at once: how many splits are certified, and how well held-out questions are routed to the right cell (no judge calls).
plain_description.why: It tests whether building per corpus and then merging gives a better multi-benchmark taxonomy than one joint build.
plain_description.information: More certified splits and good routing would favour the federated design. Result: per-corpus building recovers certification (13 certified splits vs 5 for the joint build). The grafted tree routes 72% of questions to the right cell. The loss comes from the top-level choice of which benchmark subtree to enter: assigning each question straight to the nearest cell scores 82%. No rule for the top level is shown.
